summary: Cheese pupusas are thick masa harina discs stuffed with melting cheese and cooked about 3 minutes per side on a griddle or cast-iron skillet, served with curtido, a vinegary cabbage slaw.
glance: Vegetarian and gluten-free; not vegan unless you use vegan cheese
faq: What cheese do you use for pupusas?
A soft, fresh quesillo is the most traditional. If you can't find it, any mild, meltable cheese works well, and fresh goat cheese (chevre) is also delicious, though not traditional.
Do I need a tortilla press to make pupusas?
No. Pupusas can be shaped entirely by hand, or with a tortilla press for a more uniform thickness and a neater look.
How should pupusa dough feel?
Moist and firm, like Play-Doh. You should be able to form it without cracking. Add more water a little at a time as needed, then let it rest, covered, at least 10 minutes.
How do you cook pupusas?

Fill a ball of dough about 1 3/4 inches across with about 1 1/2 tablespoons of cheese, seal it, and flatten it to about 5 inches. Cook on a lightly greased griddle or cast-iron skillet over medium heat for about 3 minutes per side until golden brown. You can hold them in a 200 degree oven while you finish the batch.
What is curtido?
Curtido is the classic accompaniment to pupusas: a simple, vinegary cabbage slaw that cuts through the richness of the filling. Let it stand at least an hour before serving.
What are other vegetarian fillings for pupusas?
Refried beans (if they don't contain lard) and loroco, a flower bud that can be hard to find in America.

summary: Romesco is a Spanish sauce of roasted red pepper, canned tomatoes, roasted garlic and toasted hazelnuts or almonds, blended with smoked paprika, sherry vinegar and oil; this version makes 1 cup in 55 minutes.
glance: Prep 15 min, cook 40 min, total 55 min
faq: What is romesco sauce made of?

Roasted red peppers, tomatoes, roasted garlic and toasted nuts. This version uses roasted red bell pepper, canned San Marzano tomatoes, hazelnuts, salt, sherry vinegar, smoked paprika and hazelnut oil or extra-virgin olive oil.
Does romesco need bread?

It is typically thickened with bread, but this version leaves it out for a thinner consistency. For a thicker romesco, toast or pan-fry one slice of rustic bread and blend it with the other ingredients.
Should I use hazelnuts or almonds?
Either works; almonds or hazelnuts are most commonly used. This recipe uses all hazelnuts, with roasted hazelnut oil for extra flavor. Without hazelnut oil, extra-virgin olive oil is still great.
How do you roast the peppers for romesco?

A blowtorch is fast and blisters the skin evenly while leaving the flesh fresher. You can also use the broiler or, very carefully, a stove burner. Rest the pepper in a covered bowl for 5 minutes, then rub off the skin.
What do you use romesco for?
As a party dip or spread, as part of a tapas-style meal, stirred into mayonnaise, or slathered on a sandwich.
Is romesco vegan?
Yes. As written it is vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free.

glance: flaky sea salt folded in after churning

summary: Sichuan peppercorn peanuts: unsalted peanuts tossed in a skillet with oil, ground Sichuan peppercorn, coriander, ancho, guajillo and orange zest for a numbing, spicy snack that keeps a few days.
glance: peanuts toss in the spiced oil for 2 minutes
faq: What do Sichuan peppercorns taste like?
They are the seed hulls of a tree in the citrus family, so they have a citrusy flavor, but their most prominent feature is a tongue-numbing zing, a bit like licking a 9-volt battery, in a good way.
How do you grind Sichuan peppercorns?
Use a mortar and pestle, an electric coffee grinder, or a ceramic hand mill such as a Hario, which lets you adjust the grind very precisely.
Can I make the peanuts hotter or more numbing?
Yes. Adjust the ratio of heat, orange zest, salt and Sichuan peppercorn to taste. The amount in the recipe isn't large, so feel free to amp up the peppercorn if you like the zing.
How long do Sichuan peppercorn peanuts keep?
A few days. Drain them on paper towels, toss with the salt, and store them for snacking.
How else can I use them?
As a snack with a beer, or tossed with crispy, pan-fried tofu for a spicy variation on kung pao.

summary: Thick, cakey chocolate chip cookies from melted butter, a splash of milk, flaky salt and dough chilled at least an hour, baked at 375°F for 9 to 11 minutes; the recipe makes 30.
glance: at least 1 hour, preferably 2 or overnight
faq: How do you make chocolate chip cookies thick and cakey?

Chill the dough well, then form compact, high balls. With less time to spread in the oven, the outer layer sets first. The recipe also melts the butter, which coats the flour and reduces gluten development that would toughen the cookie.
Why chill chocolate chip cookie dough?
Chilling is the biggest step toward cakey cookies. Refrigerate at least one hour, preferably two or overnight, until quite firm. Skip it and your cookies will be flat and hard.
How long do you bake these cookies?
Bake at 375 degrees for 9 to 11 minutes, until well risen and lightly browned around the edges.
What chocolate should I use?

The recipe uses Ghirardelli semi-sweet chips, and their 60% cacao chips are even better. You can also use good bulk chocolate chunks, and at least 25% more chocolate than the recipe calls for works fine.
Can I age the dough for 24-48 hours?
Some research says cookies come out even tastier if you age the dough 24 to 48 hours in the refrigerator. The author hasn't tried it with this recipe.
Can I reuse a hot baking sheet?
Don't. If you must, rinse it under cool water and dry it first. While one sheet bakes, you can prepare the next and refrigerate the dough balls until ready.

summary: Vietnamese green mango salad: firm, slightly underripe mango batons tossed with a sweet lime, ginger and toasted sesame oil dressing, red onion, chili, sesame seeds and herbs; it serves 4.
glance: slightly underripe: firm, but not rock hard
sweet; sesame oil stands in for fish sauce
faq: What kind of mango do you use for green mango salad?
Slightly underripe mangos: firm, but not rock hard. The recipe also notes that papaya works for this kind of salad.
How do you cut green mango for salad?
Into medium batons. The easiest way is with a mandoline, which also makes for a neater presentation, but a knife works too and just takes a little more time.
Can you make the dressing without fish sauce?

Yes. This dressing uses lime juice, palm sugar, ginger, salt and a tablespoon of toasted sesame oil. A little soy sauce often works as an umami-rich substitute elsewhere, but here the sesame oil does the job.
How sweet should the dressing be?
Fairly sweet. Taste it and adjust to balance the particular mangos you are using.
Is Vietnamese green mango salad vegan?
Yes. As written it is vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free, and it serves 4.
